source: Nuckton TJ, Alonso JA, Kallet RH, et al. Pulmonary dead-space fraction as a risk factor for death in the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med 2002; 346(17):1281-1286.
claim: Elevated alveolar dead space fraction impairs effective alveolar ventilation at standard minute ventilation, driving hypercapnia and widening the arterial-to-end-tidal carbon dioxide gradient.
failureReason: With 90s arterial tau and 60/40 tissue weighting, PaCO2 rises from 42 to only 51.1 mmHg in 90s; reaching 55 mmHg requires >180s.
